• Wild caught Betta foerschi, from the Betta foerschi complex.
  • IUCN Red List: Endangered (very high risk of extinction in the wild).
  • Temperament: somewhat territorial, but can be kept in groups as long as there is enough space.
  • Maximum size: 2.25 inches.
  • Breeding: mouthbrooder.

Imported on 5/09/25 (May 9, 2025); shipping starts on 5/19/25 (May 19, 2025). Be sure to have the habitat ready before purchase.

Mandor, foerschi and Strohi are notoriously difficult to sex at a young age; older fish with longer finnage are much easier.
We recommend a pair per 5 gallons of water.

• TDS: ~60–100 (can tolerate high TDS water but prefers low TDS water).
  • pH: ~6.0–7.0 (prefers softer water).
  • Temperature: 75–83°F (does well in cooler temperatures, but higher temperatures induce coloration and breeding behaviours).
Carnivorous. Currently feeding on live foods but can be trained to eat frozen and dried foods. We currently feed them blackworms, frozen bloodworms and pellets.

With a black base body with red bars on the opercular cheeks, females will often have gold bars, but this is NOT a defining factor for their sex. Fully grown adult males have longer anal and caudal fins compared to females. Very similar to Mandor except for a slightly smaller, slimmer body and finnage. Like many species in the complex, females show vertical bars on the body when in breeding mode.
